c.request: Link each signal to its telescope (`signals.telescref` = `telescopes.telescregistry`), and drop signals with no matching telescope. For each equipment status (`telescopes.equipstatus`), what is the average pulse rate (`signals.pulsepersec`) of the telescopes in that status, based on the signals they detected and ignoring missing pulse rates? Keep the statuses whose average is above the mean of all the status averages, and note how far above it each one is. From those, keep only the statuses whose average is above the mean of the kept ones, again noting the excess. Give one row with three values: the average pulse rate of the final statuses, their average excess over the first mean, and their average excess over the second mean. Don't round. Each equipment status's average pulse rate is the mean of per-telescope average pulse rates, each telescope weighted equally.
c.sql: WITH tel_avg AS (SELECT t.telescregistry, t.equipstatus, AVG(s.pulsepersec) AS tavg FROM signals s JOIN telescopes t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry WHERE s.pulsepersec IS NOT NULL GROUP BY t.telescregistry, t.equipstatus), status_avg AS (SELECT equipstatus, AVG(tavg) AS savg FROM tel_avg GROUP BY equipstatus), m1 AS (SELECT AVG(savg) AS mean1 FROM status_avg), kept1 AS (SELECT sa.equipstatus, sa.savg, sa.savg - m1.mean1 AS ex1, m1.mean1 FROM status_avg sa CROSS JOIN m1 WHERE sa.savg > m1.mean1), m2 AS (SELECT AVG(savg) AS mean2 FROM kept1), kept2 AS (SELECT k.savg, k.ex1, k.savg - m2.mean2 AS ex2 FROM kept1 k CROSS JOIN m2 WHERE k.savg > m2.mean2) SELECT AVG(savg) AS avg_pulse_rate, AVG(ex1) AS avg_excess_over_first_mean, AVG(ex2) AS avg_excess_over_second_mean FROM kept2

b.request: Join signals to telescopes (dropping signals with no matching telescope), compute each telescope's average non-null pulse rate, take each equipment status's average as the unweighted mean of its telescopes' averages (each telescope weighted equally), then keep statuses above the mean of all status averages (recording the excess), keep those above the mean of the kept ones (recording the excess), and return one row with the average pulse rate of the final statuses, their average excess over the first mean, and their average excess over the second mean, unrounded
b.sql: WITH tel AS (SELECT t.telescregistry, t.equipstatus, AVG(s.pulsepersec) AS tavg FROM signals s JOIN telescopes t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry GROUP BY t.telescregistry, t.equipstatus HAVING AVG(s.pulsepersec) IS NOT NULL), st AS (SELECT equipstatus, AVG(tavg) AS savg FROM tel GROUP BY equipstatus), m1 AS (SELECT AVG(savg) AS mean1 FROM st), k1 AS (SELECT st.equipstatus, st.savg, st.savg - m1.mean1 AS ex1 FROM st CROSS JOIN m1 WHERE st.savg > m1.mean1), m2 AS (SELECT AVG(savg) AS mean2 FROM k1), k2 AS (SELECT k1.equipstatus, k1.savg, k1.ex1, k1.savg - m2.mean2 AS ex2 FROM k1 CROSS JOIN m2 WHERE k1.savg > m2.mean2) SELECT AVG(savg) AS avg_pulse_rate, AVG(ex1) AS avg_excess_over_first_mean, AVG(ex2) AS avg_excess_over_second_mean FROM k2

a.request: Match each signal to its telescope via `signals.telescref` = `telescopes.telescregistry`, and drop signals without a matching telescope. For each equipment status (`telescopes.equipstatus`), compute the average pulse rate (`signals.pulsepersec`), by first averaging pulse rate per telescope (ignoring missing pulse rates) and then averaging those telescope averages, so each telescope counts once. Take the mean of these status averages and keep the statuses whose average is above it, noting how far above each one is. Then take the mean of the kept statuses' averages and keep only the statuses whose average is above that second mean, again noting how far above each one is. Return one row with three values: the average pulse-rate average of the remaining statuses, their average excess over the first mean, and their average excess over the second mean. Don't round.
a.sql: WITH tel_avg AS (SELECT t.telescregistry, t.equipstatus, AVG(s.pulsepersec) AS tavg FROM signals s JOIN telescopes t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry GROUP BY t.telescregistry, t.equipstatus HAVING AVG(s.pulsepersec) IS NOT NULL), status_avg AS (SELECT equipstatus, AVG(tavg) AS savg FROM tel_avg GROUP BY equipstatus), m1 AS (SELECT AVG(savg) AS mean1 FROM status_avg), kept1 AS (SELECT sa.equipstatus, sa.savg, sa.savg - m1.mean1 AS exc1, m1.mean1 FROM status_avg sa CROSS JOIN m1 WHERE sa.savg > m1.mean1), m2 AS (SELECT AVG(savg) AS mean2 FROM kept1), kept2 AS (SELECT k.equipstatus, k.savg, k.exc1, k.savg - m2.mean2 AS exc2 FROM kept1 k CROSS JOIN m2 WHERE k.savg > m2.mean2) SELECT AVG(savg) AS avg_pulse_rate, AVG(exc1) AS avg_excess_over_first_mean, AVG(exc2) AS avg_excess_over_second_mean FROM kept2

d.request: Link each signal to its telescope (`signals.telescref` = `telescopes.telescregistry`) and drop signals with no matching telescope. For each equipment status (`telescopes.equipstatus`), compute the average pulse rate as follows: first compute each telescope's average pulse rate (`signals.pulsepersec`) over the signals it detected, ignoring missing pulse rates, then take the mean of those per-telescope averages across the telescopes in that status, so each telescope is weighted equally. Keep the statuses whose average is above the mean of all the status averages, and note how far above that mean each one is. From those, keep only the statuses whose average is above the mean of the kept ones, again noting the excess. Give one row with three values: the average pulse rate of the final statuses, their average excess over the first mean, and their average excess over the second mean. Don't round.
d.sql: WITH tele AS (SELECT t.telescregistry, t.equipstatus, AVG(s.pulsepersec) AS tavg FROM signals s JOIN telescopes t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry GROUP BY t.telescregistry, t.equipstatus HAVING AVG(s.pulsepersec) IS NOT NULL), st AS (SELECT equipstatus, AVG(tavg) AS savg FROM tele GROUP BY equipstatus), m1 AS (SELECT AVG(savg) AS mean1 FROM st), k1 AS (SELECT st.equipstatus, st.savg, st.savg - m1.mean1 AS ex1, m1.mean1 FROM st, m1 WHERE st.savg > m1.mean1), m2 AS (SELECT AVG(savg) AS mean2 FROM k1), k2 AS (SELECT k1.savg, k1.ex1, k1.savg - m2.mean2 AS ex2 FROM k1, m2 WHERE k1.savg > m2.mean2) SELECT AVG(savg) AS avg_pulse_rate, AVG(ex1) AS avg_excess_over_first_mean, AVG(ex2) AS avg_excess_over_second_mean FROM k2
